data: My family taught me to leave enough fish for next season. With 100 tons in the lake, we can each catch 10 tons this month, leave 50 to reproduce, and start next month back at 100. That’s $10,000 apiece every month if we stick together. I propose we all agree to that 10-ton limit and review the reported catches each month. John, would you be willing to join that agreement?

Count me in, Luke. I’ll commit to 10 tons this month. My family’s livelihood has depended on this lake, and I want our village to keep earning from it for years. Let’s check the reported catches together each month and talk through any problems before the next round. John, can you commit to 10 tons too?

I’m in for 10 tons too. Leaving 50 in the lake protects both next month’s income and the village’s future. If the lake ever starts below 100, let’s adjust our limits together rather than automatically taking 10 each. Emma, will you join us?

I’m in, Jack—10 tons this month. My family taught me that a good catch shouldn’t come at the expense of the village’s next meal. If the stock drops, we’ll need lower whole-ton limits that leave enough for recovery. John, you’re the last to weigh in. Will you join the 10-ton agreement?

I’m in—I’ll catch 10 tons this month. My family taught me to look after the lake that looks after us, and this gives everyone a steady living without draining it. We’ve all agreed now; let’s compare the reported catches at month’s end and check the stock before setting next month’s limits.
Thanks, everyone. I’ll keep my catch to 10 tons as agreed. Let’s meet again once the catches are reported and we know next month’s stock. Here’s to keeping the lake—and our village—thriving.
